# Harrison

## Overview

- **Age:** Middle-aged  <sub>[v2 c13 P7](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0007)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- **Status:** Alive  <sub>[v2 c30 P4](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0004)</sub>
- **Origin:** New Brunswick  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- **Role:** Farmer  <sub>[v2 c13 P7](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0007), [v2 c17 P8](../source/v02-c17.md#nw-v02-c17-p0008)</sub>

## Appearance

Mr. Harrison is a short, fat, and bald man with a round face and prominent blue eyes. When enraged, his face turns purple and his eyes protrude severely. Following his wife's return, his appearance changes significantly to look neat and snug, occasionally wearing a white collar when attempting to appear prosperous.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P11](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0011), [v2 c17 P76](../source/v02-c17.md#nw-v02-c17-p0076), [v2 c17 P78](../source/v02-c17.md#nw-v02-c17-p0078), [v2 c28 P8](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0008)_

## Personality

Outwardly outspoken, fidgety, crusty, and cantankerous, Mr. Harrison prides himself on his blunt frankness, though he is inherently kind and sympathetic. He prefers a quiet, placid life without fuss or excessive tidiness, though he can be stubborn and cranky when nagged. He enjoys social visits, likes young people, and strongly dislikes being pitied or dealing with gossip.

_Sources: [v2 c3 P39](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0039), [v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049), [v2 c4 P28](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0028), [v2 c9 P40](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0040), [v2 c17 P8](../source/v02-c17.md#nw-v02-c17-p0008), [v2 c17 P78](../source/v02-c17.md#nw-v02-c17-p0078), [v2 c20 P8](../source/v02-c20.md#nw-v02-c20-p0008), [v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)_

## History

In early April, Mr. J. A. Harrison bought Robert Bell's farm in Avonlea and moved there from New Brunswick. He initially kept house by himself without regular meal times and gained a reputation among the locals as an odd crank. After an initial confrontation with Anne Shirley over a Jersey cow, the two quickly became close friends, often spending evenings conversing on his veranda. He supported the Village Improvement Society and proved himself to be a kind, sympathetic neighbor despite his rough exterior. Later, his estranged wife Emily joined him in Avonlea after his parrot Ginger died, reuniting the couple. Following their reconciliation, Mr. Harrison began attending church every Sunday, subscribing to the minister's salary, and keeping a far neater appearance.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P6](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0006), [v2 c3 P39](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0039), [v2 c4 P28](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0028), [v2 c6 P56](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0056), [v2 c9 P40](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0040), [v2 c25 P47](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0047), [v2 c25 P59](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0059), [v2 c28 P8](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0008)_

## Background by volume

- Lived in Scottsford, New Brunswick before moving to Avonlea  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- Promised his dying sister he would marry Emily Scott  <sub>[v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>
- Separated from his wife after constant bickering over neatness and his parrot, Ginger  <sub>[v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057), [v2 c25 P59](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0059)</sub>
- Inherited his late sailor brother's parrot, Ginger  <sub>[v2 c25 P57](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0057)</sub>

## Quotes

> I’m a crusty, lonesome, crabbed old chap, but there’s something about that little girl makes me feel young again . . . and it’s such a pleasant sensation I’d like to have it repeated once in a while.  <sub>[v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049)</sub>

> That old nuisance of a Rachel Lynde was here again today, pestering me for a subscription towards buying a carpet for the vestry room. I detest that woman more than anybody I know. She can put a whole sermon, text, comment, and application, into six words, and throw it at you like a brick.  <sub>[v2 c9 P0](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0000)</sub>

> Emily’s gone over to Carmody with Rachel Lynde . . . she’s struck up a lifelong friendship already with Rachel Lynde. Beats all how contrary women are. Well, Anne, my easy times are over . . . all over. It’s neatness and tidiness for me for the rest of my natural life, I suppose.  <sub>[v2 c25 P47](../source/v02-c25.md#nw-v02-c25-p0047)</sub>

> Well, we’re going to miss you an awful lot, Emily and me. To be sure, Mrs. Lynde’ll be over there in your place. There ain’t nobody but a substitute can be found for them.  <sub>[v2 c30 P4](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0004)</sub>
